title: progressive-hedging-and-regional-affinity-for-rerank
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Background: Several high-traffic customers and internal benchmarks have exposed two recurring failure modes in the reranking endpoint: 1) transient latency spikes from overloaded GPU pools in a region causing user-facing timeouts; 2) long tails where a single slow host or a cold KV cache causes cascading slowdowns and higher cost. Current fallbacks are coarse-grained and either over-eager (downgrading quality unnecessarily) or too slow to prevent SLO breaches.

Proposal: Implement a progressive hedging + regional-affinity routing strategy for reranker requests that balances quality, latency, and cost. Key parts: (A) Adaptive per-request hedging windows: for requests exceeding a percentile-based latency threshold we issue a hedged request to a warm alternative pool (regional or dedicated) after a short adaptive delay; (B) Progressive fallback tiers: quality-preserving fallbacks ordered by compatibility (same-model same-quantization -> lighter quantized variant -> cached local result -> degraded scorer) rather than immediate downgrade to a compact variant; (C) Regional affinity with latency-aware routing: route primary requests to the preferred region based on trace-level latency history and capacity signals, but allow cross-region hedges when local queues/backpressure indicate risk; (D) Circuit-breaker stitches: per-pool and per-model circuit-breakers driven by real-time p50/p95/p99 latency and error-rate windows with automated short-circuiting to fallback tier; (E) Cache-aware hedging: consult embedding/reranker KV cache state in routing decisions and prefetch promising keys for warmups; (F) Observability and SLOs: new metrics, dashboards and alerting for hedged request ratios, hedge-replacement benefit, and cost delta.

Why this is different: instead of binary canary/fallback rules, this is a staged, signal-driven mitigation system that targets the long tail, preserves top-tier quality when possible, and bounds cost via adaptive hedging thresholds and breaker budgets.
acceptance_criteria: Hedging mechanism implemented in reranker service with config flags to enable/disable per-customer and global policies
Progressive fallback chain implemented and unit-tested with mock compatibility checks
Regional affinity routing uses per-route latency history and falls back to cross-region hedges if local p95 > configured SLO
Circuit-breakers trigger and recover predictably based on real-time latency/error windows (integration tests)
End-to-end integration test demonstrates p99 reduction on synthetic tail-burst workload by >=40% with cost delta <=6%
Dashboards created: Hedge Ratio, Hedge Win Rate, P99 with and without hedges, Cost per 1M tokens for rerank path
Canary rollout plan and rollback hook documented; no customer-facing incidents during canary on 20% of production traffic for 72h
design_notes: Hedge delay will be computed per-model using exponential backoff around the model's baseline p95 latency; we will calibrate at start with historical traces
Circuit-breakers are scoped: (pool, model_variant, tenant). We will use sliding windows of 1m/5m for different reactions (fast short-circuit vs sustained open)
Fallback chain uses compatibility metadata attached to model manifests; default chain defined in runtime and overridable via per-tenant policy
Cost control: cap concurrent hedges per-tenant and apply budget accounting to avoid runaway costs during platform-wide incidents
Regional affinity keeps sticky preference for low-latency regions but decays after a configurable TTL to avoid hot-spotting
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (Spike, 1 week): implement prototype hedging path and toggles in a shadow rerun mode; gather traces and calibrate thresholds
Phase 2 (Core, 3 weeks): add progressive fallback chain logic, model manifest compatibility checks, and per-pool circuit-breaker service
Phase 3 (Routing, 2 weeks): integrate regional affinity signals into router, enable cross-region hedges and capacity checks
Phase 4 (Canary, 1 week): rollout to 10-20% traffic with detailed telemetry, iterate thresholds
Phase 5 (Rollout, 1 week): progressive ramp to 100% and postmortem/lessons-learned
monitoring_and_alerts: Modify existing SLO alerts to consider hedged and non-hedged p99 separately
Add budget alerts for hedging cost delta crossing 8% sustained over 30m
Create daily job to audit per-tenant hedge usage and suggest config recommendations
rollout_plan: Start in internal staging with synthetic tail-burst tests
Canary to < 5 customers (20% traffic) for 72h with monitoring and on-call runbook
Progressively increase to 50% then 100% after verification
Immediate disable knob in console and API for emergency rollback
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Hedging increases cost under sustained high latency - Mitigation: budget caps and dynamic disable when cost alarms fire
Risk: Cross-region hedges may violate data residency - Mitigation: respect tenant routing policies and honor per-tenant region allowlists
Risk: Complexity increases operational toil - Mitigation: provide curated presets and automated suggestions from Redwood Optimize
comments: 2026-03-02 Priya Shah: Spike started. Collected baseline p50/p95/p99 traces from last 30 days across US/EU clusters.
2026-03-04 Marco Duarte: Early prototype shows p99 drop of 28% in staging for short bursts with naive hedging; planning to add progressive fallback next.
2026-03-07 Security review: confirmed cross-region hedges require tenant allowlist; adding per-tenant region policy toggle.
2026-03-09 QA: integration tests for fallback chain flapping added. Found an edge case where compatibility metadata absent causes fallback skip — added default safe-chain.
2026-03-10 Marco Duarte: Canary scheduled for 2026-03-11 to 2026-03-14 on 3 production customers; runbook and rollback documented in Confluence
